To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mice presensitized with Mtb TDM and challenged with the same TDM develop a hypersensitivity reaction, whereas presensitized and challenged mice with M. bobis-derived TDM do not.

mice presensitized to Mtb-derived TDCM (cord factor) followed by a challenge with the same TDCM species resulted in elicited hypersensitivity reactions, which were significantly stronger than when mice were challenged with TDCM from a different mycobacterial strain (M. bovis).
Mtb-derived trealose 6, 6'-dimyoclate (TDM; a glycolipid component of cord factor) is more inflammatory in vivo than TDM derived from M. bovis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

elucidating the mechanisms by which TDM elicits hypersensitive inflammatory reactions, as well as the role that these hypersensitive responses play in the development of chronic pulmonary disease in tuberculosis.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of immune responses to Trehalose 6, 6'-dimyoclate (TDM) in mice.

the development of a novel immunization approach for Mtb, using TDM as an adjuvant, which is based on the development of hypersensitivity to the homologus TDM, and which is designed to induce protective immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TDM derived from Mtb and M. bovis are immunologically distinct, and that the Mtb-derived glycolipid is a potent inducer of hypersensitive responses.
the hypersensitive immune response to the homologuous TDM is a result of the presence of a unique species-specific TDM epitope.
Mtb-derived TMD contains a hypersensitive epitope(s) that is not present on Mtb-derived TMS, and that this epitope(s) may be responsible for the unique hypersensitive immune responses observed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mtb-derived TMD has unique species-specific epitopes that are recognized by the host immune system, and that these epitopes are responsible for eliciting stronger hypersensitive responses in mice.

the Mtb-derived trehaldose dimycolate is a more potent inflammatory agent than the M. bovus-derived trehalose dimycolat, and that the Mtb derived trehalose dimycloate is more immunogenic than the M. bous derived trehalose diycloate.
the Mtb-derived cord factor contains a unique species-specific epitope not present on the M. bovus-derived cord factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are unique species-specific epitopes on TDM, and these epitopes may contribute to the pathogenesis of Mtb.
there is an immunological difference in TDM from M. bovis and M. tuberculosis, and that this difference may be important to the immune response to tuberculosis.
there are differences in hypersensitivity to mycobacterial glycolipids, with the Mtb TDM eliciting a more severe hypersensitive response than M. bovis.
